This file IS the source document, so `transcribed_from` names its own path: it is the artefact under review, not a transcription of one. The volume was supplied as one combined PDF and cut into parts at its own headings, so this file is a page-range slice of a single extraction and its page ids (PDF pages None–None, no printed page numbers on these pages) are the combined document's own, not renumbered from 0. Front matter (cover and title page, contents, list of sections, foreword, statement of policy, personnel, correspondence, summary of changes, cross-referencing) and back matter (back cover) were deleted from the drop before supply and are NOT filed; the drop's `content.json`, `index.json`, `meta.json` and `README.md` are retained beside the kind folders, unfiled, for the same reason. SPECIFICATION FOR NICKEL-CHROMIUM-MOLYBDENUM-COLUMBIUM ALLOY (UNS N06625) AND NICKEL-CHROMIUM-MOLYBDENUM-SILICON ALLOY (UNS N06219) PLATE, SHEET, AND STRIP
[Identical with ASTM Specification B 443-00(2014) except that certification has been made mandatory.]
1.1 This specification covers rolled nickel-chromiummolybdenum-columbium alloy (UNS N06625) and nickelchromium-molybdenum-silicon alloy (UNS N06219) plate, sheet, and strip.
1.1.1 Alloy UNS N06625 products are furnished in two grades of different heat-treated conditions:
1.1.1.1 Grade 1 (Annealed)— Material is normally employed in service temperatures up to 1100°F (593°C).

1.1.1.2 Grade 2 (Solution Annealed)— Material is normally employed in service temperatures above 1100°F (593°C) when resistance to creep and rupture is required. NOTE 1 — Hot-working or reannealing may change properties significantly, depending on working history and temperatures.
1.1.2 Alloy UNS N06219 is supplied in solution annealed condition only.
1.2 The values stated in inch-pound units are to be regarded as the standard. The values given in parentheses are for information only.

7.1.1 Plate— For plate up to 2 in. (50.8 mm), inclusive, in thickness, the permissible variations under the specified thickness and permissible excess in overweight shall not exceed the amounts prescribed in Table 4.
7.1.1.1 For use with Table 4, plate shall be assumed to weigh 0.305 lb/in.3 (8.442 g/cm3 ).

7.1.3 Sheet and Strip — The permissible variations in thickness of sheet and strip shall be as prescribed in Table 6. The thickness of strip and sheet shall be measured with the micrometer spindle 3 ⁄ 8 in. (9.5 mm) or more from either edge for material 1 in. 7.2.1 Plate— The permissible variations in width of rectangular plates and diameter of circular plates shall be as prescribed in Table 7 and Table 8.
7.2.2 Sheet and Strip— The permissible variations in width for sheet and strip shall be as prescribed in Table 9.
7.3.1 Sheet and strip of all sizes may be ordered to cut lengths, in which case a variation of 1 ⁄ 8 in. (3.2 mm) over the specified length shall be permitted.
7.3.2 Permissible variations in length of rectangular plate shall be as prescribed in Table 10.
7.4.1 The edgewise curvature (depth of chord) of flat sheet, strip, and plate shall not exceed 0.05 in. (1.27 mm) multiplied by the length in feet (0.04 mm multiplied by the length in centimeters).
7.4.2 Straightness for coiled material is subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser.
